subtopics.title: Two Kinds of Change — the Deciding Question

questions.question: The single question that classifies any change is:
options: Did the change release energy?
Is a new substance formed?
Was the change fast or slow?
Did the substance change colour?

questions.question: Chocolate melting in your pocket is a physical change because:
options: It absorbs body heat
It changes shape as it softens
It happens slowly
No new substance forms — melted chocolate is still chocolate, and cooling sets it again

questions.question: When a match is struck and burns, the change is chemical because:
options: Bonds break and new bonds form — the atoms regroup into smoke, gases and a blackened stump
The match gets hot
The match changes shape
The flame moves quickly

questions.question: Chemical changes are usually hard to reverse because:
options: They always need a flame
The original substance no longer exists — it has been rebuilt into new substances
They only happen in laboratories
The particles move too fast to catch

subtopics.title: Physical Change Up Close — Same Particles, New Arrangement

questions.question: Washing drying on the line is a physical change because:
options: The sun's energy destroys the water
The fabric changes texture
The intact water molecules simply gain enough energy to leave as vapour — no new substance forms
The water reacts with the fabric

questions.question: Dissolving Epsom salts in water is physical because:
options: Every ion and water molecule survives unchanged — evaporation returns identical crystals
The crystals are destroyed by the water
Salt water is a brand-new substance
The change releases heat

questions.question: Sand stirred into salt forms a mixture, not a new substance, because:
options: Sand and salt have the same particles
The mixture is dry
Mixtures always look uniform
Both can be recovered unchanged — dissolve the salt, filter the sand, evaporate the water

questions.question: An energy change during melting proves:
options: Nothing about classification on its own — physical changes also absorb or release energy; only a new substance proves chemistry
That the change must be chemical
That mass has been lost
That the change cannot be reversed

subtopics.title: Chemical Change Up Close — New Substances, and the Evidence

questions.question: The five signs of chemical change are:
options: Melting, freezing, boiling, condensing, subliming
Stirring, filtering, heating, cooling, evaporating
Gas produced, precipitate formed, permanent colour change, self-caused temperature change, light or sound emitted
Shine, hardness, texture, smell, taste

questions.question: A precipitate is:
options: An insoluble solid that appears when two clear solutions react
The solid left after evaporating a solution
A gas escaping from a liquid
Any solid that dissolves easily

questions.question: A hand warmer heating itself, and sherbet turning your tongue cold, are respectively:
options: Endothermic and exothermic
Physical and chemical
Reversible and irreversible
Exothermic and endothermic

questions.question: Bubbles alone do not prove a chemical change because:
options: Bubbles are too small to test
Boiling water also bubbles, and boiling is physical — the verdict still needs a new substance
Gases never take part in reactions
Bubbles only form in acids

subtopics.title: Mass, Energy and the Tricky Cases

questions.question: Steel wool burned in oxygen leaves ash that weighs MORE than the metal did. Conservation of mass still holds because:
options: Heat has weight
The law does not apply to metals
Oxygen from the air joined the iron — count the oxygen on the input side and the totals match exactly
The steel wool absorbed water

questions.question: Boiling water versus passing an electric current through water:
options: Boiling is physical — steam is still water; electrolysis is chemical — hydrogen and oxygen are new substances
Both are physical changes
Both are chemical changes
Boiling is chemical; electrolysis is physical

questions.question: Sugar heated in a pan first melts, then darkens into caramel and black carbon. The correct classification is:
options: Both stages are physical because sugar is edible
Both stages are chemical because heat was involved
Melting is chemical; browning is physical
Melting is physical; the browning is chemical — caramel and carbon are new substances that never turn back into white sugar

questions.question: Bubbles from a just-opened fizzy drink are a physical change because:
options: The gas was already dissolved in the liquid and is simply escaping — nothing new was made
The drink reacts with the air
Carbon dioxide is not a real substance
The bubbles are made of water vapour

subtopics.title: The Ice Tray and the Braai Fire

questions.question: The ice tray scene shows physical change because the water:
options: Loses a little mass each cycle
Can be frozen and melted over and over, staying water at every stage
Becomes a new substance in the freezer
Cannot be melted once frozen

questions.question: The braai fire scene shows chemical change because the wood:
options: Changes shape in the flames
Gets extremely hot
No longer exists — it has become ash, smoke and gases, and no simple process brings it back
Is preserved inside the ash

questions.question: The take-home test from the two scenes is:
options: If the original can be recovered by simple means — cooling, evaporating, filtering, sieving — the change was physical
If the change needed a fire, it was chemical
If the change happened in a kitchen, it was physical
If the change was slow, it was physical

questions.question: Rising bread dough is a chemical clue because:
options: The dough gets warmer in the kitchen
The yeast is making new carbon dioxide gas that was never in the flour
The dough changes shape
Flour always expands when wet

questions.question: A cut avocado browning on the plate is evidence of chemical change because the colour:
options: Matches the colour of the skin
Rinses off under the tap
Only appears in sunlight
Goes deep and will not come back — a new substance has formed at the surface

questions.question: The fizzy-drink bubbles remind the detective that:
options: A single clue can mislead — that gas was already dissolved, so its escape is physical; conviction needs a new substance
All bubbles prove chemistry
Fizzy drinks are chemical changes in a bottle
Dissolved gases do not exist

subtopics.title: The Candle Doing Both at Once

questions.question: The wax melting at the top of a burning candle is:
options: Chemical — the flame transforms the wax
Physical — the drop that runs down the side cools and hardens back into wax, unchanged
Chemical — heat always means chemistry
Neither physical nor chemical

questions.question: The wax burning at the wick is chemical because it:
options: Climbs the wick as a liquid
Glows brightly
Combines with oxygen to become carbon dioxide and water vapour — new substances that never return to wax
Gets used up slowly

questions.question: Weighing the candle before and after, capturing all the gases and counting the oxygen used, shows:
options: The flame destroys a small amount of mass
Only the wick loses mass
Mass increases because light is absorbed
The ledger balances exactly — atoms regroup but never vanish: conservation of mass
